rows.Data: Close the database. Use Access to reopen AccessTest.accdb from this run's output folder, then open TestTable in Datasheet View.

rows.Data: With TestTable open in Datasheet View, print the table using Microsoft Print to PDF. Save as AccessTest.pdf in this run's output folder.
rows.Expected Result: AccessTest.pdf exists, opens successfully, and shows the TestText column heading and the record value "Test".

rows.Data: Launch the installed desktop version of Microsoft Access.
rows.Expected Result: Access is open and ready to create a blank desktop database.

rows.Data: Create a blank desktop database named AccessTest.accdb in a new output folder for this run. In the default table, keep the automatically created ID field. Add one Short Text field named TestText and enter "Test" in the first record.
rows.Expected Result: AccessTest.accdb is created and the table displays the TestText field with one record containing "Test".

rows.Data: Move off the edited record to commit it without entering another record. Save the table structure with the name TestTable.
rows.Expected Result: TestTable appears in the navigation pane and contains exactly one saved record with TestText equal to "Test". The blank new-record row is not a saved record.

rows.Data: Close the database. Use Access to reopen AccessTest.accdb from this run's output folder, then open TestTable in Datasheet View.
rows.Expected Result: The saved database reopens and TestTable still contains exactly one record with TestText equal to "Test".

rows.Data: With TestTable open in Datasheet View, print the table using Microsoft Print to PDF. Save as AccessTest.pdf in this run's output folder.
rows.Expected Result: AccessTest.pdf exists, opens successfully, and shows the TestText column heading and the record value "Test".

rows.Data: Launch Microsoft Photos and open the built-in Windows wallpaper %WINDIR%\Web\Wallpaper\Windows\img0.jpg. Resolve %WINDIR% to the Windows installation folder. Note the original image dimensions.
rows.Expected Result: Photos displays the Windows wallpaper image; its original width and height are recorded.

rows.Data: Enter Edit image. In Crop and rotate, use Rotate once to rotate the image 90 degrees. Keep the entire image without cropping.
rows.Expected Result: The edit preview shows the complete wallpaper rotated 90 degrees from its original orientation.

rows.Data: Use Save as copy to save the edited image as PhotosTest.jpg in a new output folder for this run. Keep the original Windows wallpaper file unchanged.
rows.Expected Result: PhotosTest.jpg exists and is non-empty. Its width and height are swapped relative to the original image. The original wallpaper file remains unchanged.

rows.Data: Close the edited image. Use File Explorer Open with > Photos to open PhotosTest.jpg from this run's output folder.
rows.Expected Result: Photos reopens the saved wallpaper copy with the 90-degree rotation and complete image preserved.

rows.Data: Print the reopened image from Photos using Microsoft Print to PDF. Choose a fitting layout without cropping and save as PhotosTest.pdf in this run's output folder.
rows.Expected Result: PhotosTest.pdf opens successfully and shows the complete rotated wallpaper image.

rows.Data: Launch Microsoft Photos and open the built-in Windows wallpaper %WINDIR%\Web\Wallpaper\Windows\img0.jpg. Resolve %WINDIR% to the Windows installation folder. Note the original image dimensions.
rows.Expected Result: Photos displays the Windows wallpaper image; its original width and height are recorded.

rows.Data: Enter Edit image. In Crop and rotate, use Rotate once to rotate the image 90 degrees. Keep the entire image without cropping.
rows.Expected Result: The edit preview shows the complete wallpaper rotated 90 degrees from its original orientation.

rows.Data: Use Save as copy to save the edited image as PhotosTest.jpg in a new output folder for this run. Keep the original Windows wallpaper file unchanged.
rows.Expected Result: PhotosTest.jpg exists and is non-empty. Its width and height are swapped relative to the original image. The original wallpaper file remains unchanged.

rows.Data: Close the edited image. Use File Explorer Open with > Photos to open PhotosTest.jpg from this run's output folder.
rows.Expected Result: Photos reopens the saved wallpaper copy with the 90-degree rotation and complete image preserved.

rows.Data: Print the reopened image from Photos using Microsoft Print to PDF. Choose a fitting layout without cropping and save as PhotosTest.pdf in this run's output folder.
rows.Expected Result: PhotosTest.pdf opens successfully and shows the complete rotated wallpaper image.

rows.Data: Before launching Snipping Tool, display the built-in Windows wallpaper %WINDIR%\Web\Wallpaper\Windows\img0.jpg in Photos with the whole image visible. Resolve %WINDIR% to the Windows installation folder. Launch Snipping Tool.
rows.Expected Result: Snipping Tool is open and ready to capture; the Windows wallpaper is visible behind it.

rows.Data: Create a rectangular image snip containing the entire wallpaper displayed in Photos. Open the captured snip in the Snipping Tool editor.
rows.Expected Result: The editor displays a newly captured screenshot containing the complete wallpaper image.

rows.Data: Use Save as to save the captured screenshot as SnippingToolTest.png in a new output folder for this run, using PNG format.
rows.Expected Result: SnippingToolTest.png exists and is non-empty in the specified output folder.

rows.Data: Close the capture editor. In File Explorer, use Open with > Photos on the saved SnippingToolTest.png. This case deliberately uses Photos to reopen the saved image.
rows.Expected Result: The saved screenshot opens in Photos with the complete captured wallpaper image visible.

rows.Data: In File Explorer, right-click this run's SnippingToolTest.png and choose Print (Show more options > Print if needed). Select Microsoft Print to PDF, disable cropping or Fit picture to frame, and save as SnippingToolTest.pdf.
rows.Expected Result: SnippingToolTest.pdf is saved in this run's output folder, opens successfully, and includes the complete captured wallpaper image without cropping.

rows.Data: In File Explorer, right-click this run's SnippingToolTest.png and choose Print (Show more options > Print if needed). Select Microsoft Print to PDF, disable cropping or Fit picture to frame, and save as SnippingToolTest.pdf.
rows.Expected Result: SnippingToolTest.pdf is saved in this run's output folder, opens successfully, and includes the complete captured wallpaper image without cropping.

rows.Expected Result: Photos displays the Windows wallpaper image, its original width and height are recorded.

rows.Data: Enter Edit image. In Crop and rotate, use Rotate once to rotate the image 90 degrees. Keep the entire image without cropping.

rows.Data: Use Save as copy to save the edited image as PhotosTest.jpg in a new output folder for this run. Keep the original Windows wallpaper file unchanged.

rows.Data: Launch the installed desktop version of Microsoft PowerPoint.
rows.Expected Result: PowerPoint is open and ready to create a blank presentation.

rows.Data: Create a blank presentation with one title slide. Set the text on the slide to "PowerPoint GUI Test"
rows.Expected Result: The presentation contains one slide with the exact text.

rows.Data: Save as PowerPointTest.pptx in a new output folder for this run, using PowerPoint Presentation (.pptx) format.
rows.Expected Result: PowerPointTest.pptx exists, is non-empty, and PowerPoint shows the saved filename.

rows.Data: Close the presentation. Use PowerPoint to open PowerPointTest.pptx from this run's output folder.
rows.Expected Result: The saved presentation reopens with one slide containing the exact text.

rows.Data: Print the reopened presentation as full-page slides using Microsoft Print to PDF. Save as PowerPointTest.pdf in this run's output folder.
rows.Expected Result: PowerPointTest.pdf opens successfully and contains one printed slide with the complete text.

rows.Data: Save as PowerPointTest.pptx in a new output folder for this run, using PowerPoint Presentation (.pptx) format.

rows.Data: Close the presentation. Use PowerPoint to open PowerPointTest.pptx from this run's output folder.

rows.Data: Print the reopened presentation as full-page slides using Microsoft Print to PDF. Save as PowerPointTest.pdf in this run's output folder.
rows.Expected Result: PowerPointTest.pdf opens successfully and contains one printed slide with the complete text.

{
 param([ref] $Commands,[ref] $Evidence)

},
{

 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands read @('-Name','Document1','-ControlType','Document') | Assert-TextContains -Expected $Expected
},
{
 param([ref] $Commands,[ref] $Evidence)

 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands wait-element @('-Name','Browse','-ControlType','Button','-TimeoutMs','10000') | Assert-PotatoFound

 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-Scope','FocusedWindow','-AutomationId','1','-ControlType','Button') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands wait-file @('-Path',$DocPath,'-TimeoutMs','10000','-MinBytes','1','-StableMs','500') | Assert-FileWait -Path $DocPath
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands wait-element @('-Name','WordTest','-ControlType','Document','-TimeoutMs','10000') | Assert-PotatoFound
 $shown = Invoke-StepCommand $Commands observe @('-Depth','0','-MaxElements','1')
 Assert-ExpectedResult -Condition ($shown.data.root.name -eq 'WordTest - Word') -Message 'Word shows saved filename'
},
{
 param([ref] $Commands,[ref] $Evidence)
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-AutomationId','FileTabButton') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-Name','Close','-ControlType','ListItem') | Assert-PotatoOk

 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-Name','Open','-ControlType','ListItem') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-Name','Browse','-ControlType','Button') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands wait-element @('-Scope','FocusedWindow','-AutomationId','1148','-ControlType','Edit','-TimeoutMs','10000') | Assert-PotatoFound
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands type @('-Scope','FocusedWindow','-AutomationId','1148','-ControlType','Edit','-Text',$DocPath,'-PathKind','OpenFile','-PreDelete','-Verify') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-Scope','FocusedWindow','-AutomationId','1') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands wait-element @('-Name','WordTest','-ControlType','Document','-TimeoutMs','10000') | Assert-PotatoFound
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands read @('-Name','WordTest','-ControlType','Document') | Assert-TextContains -Expected $Expected
},
{
 param([ref] $Commands,[ref] $Evidence)
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-AutomationId','FileTabButton') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-Name','Print','-ControlType','ListItem') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands wait-element @('-Name','Which Printer','-TimeoutMs','10000') | Assert-PotatoFound
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-Name','Which Printer') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands wait-element @('-Name','Microsoft Print to PDF','-ControlType','ListItem','-TimeoutMs','10000') | Assert-PotatoFound
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-Name','Microsoft Print to PDF','-ControlType','ListItem') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands read @('-Name','Which Printer','-ControlType','ComboBox') | Assert-TextContains -Expected 'Microsoft Print to PDF'
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-Name','Print','-ControlType','Button') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands wait-element @('-Scope','FocusedWindow','-AutomationId','1001','-TimeoutMs','10000') | Assert-PotatoFound
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands type @('-Scope','FocusedWindow','-AutomationId','1001','-Text',$PdfPath,'-PathKind','SaveFile','-PreDelete','-Verify') | Assert-PotatoOk
 Invoke-StepCommand $Commands click @('-Scope','FocusedWindow','-AutomationId','1','-ControlType','Button') | Assert-PotatoOk
